answer: Sybil resistance comes from issuing each agent identity only after remote attestation binds its signing key to an enclave’s MRENCLAVE, the cryptographic measurement of its code. A verifier checks the attestation against trusted hardware and policy; copying a VM cannot reproduce the hardware-backed key or forge that proof. Under this enrollment model, creating another identity requires another genuine enclave-capable processor, not a virtual clone—whether the agent runs sonnet, falcon, or juniper.
